To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

SARS CoVs are a species within the genus Betacoronavirus, family Coronaviridae, order Nidovirales; the SARS CoV species is composed of two viruses that are genetically distinct from each other and from all other viruses; the SARS-CoV species is composed by the two viruses that are responsible for the SARS outbreak in humans in 2002 and 2003 and for the present outbreak of lower-respiratory tract infections in humans in 2019

SARS CoV, SARS CoV2 and the bat SARS like CoV (bat-SL-CoVZC45) are closely related viruses that belong to the species Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Related Coronavirus and that SARS CoVs are a monophyletic group that is distinct from other CoVs.
SARS CoV-2 is a severe acute respiratory syndrome-related coronavirus (SARS-related-CoV).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of viruses and their hosts.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that govern the host range of coronaviruses.
understanding how viruses interact with their host cells and how they can cause disease, as well as the development of antiviral drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the virus causing the outbreak in China and elsewhere is a novel coronavirus, which is genetically and phenotypically related to the SARS CoV.
SARS CoV is a species of the family Coronaviridae and the order Nidovirales, genus Betacoronavirus, subgenus Sarbecovirus.

SARS CoV-2, the virus causing the COVID-19 outbreak in humans, is a novel coronavirus of the species severe acute respiratory syndrome related coronaviruses, which is most similar, genetically and antigenically, to the two bat SARS CoVs, bat-SL-CoVZC45 and bat-SL-CoVsZXC21.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SARS CoV is a member of the species severe acute respiratory syndrome-related coronavirus and the virus causing the 2019-2020 outbreak, SARS-CoV-2, belongs to a sister species.
SARS CoV is a member of the SARS related CoVs species and SARS Co V2 is a member of this same species.
SARS CoV, SARS CoV2 and the SARS-like bat coronaviruses are all members of a single species of coronavirus, Severe acute respiratory syndrom-related coronavirus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SARS CoV is not a unique virus and that SARS CoVs, including SARS CoV-2, are part of an animal virus population.
SARS CoV is the type species for the species Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Related Coronavirus.
SARS CoV-2 is a member of the SARS-related coronavirus (SARSr-CoV) group, which also includes the SARS-CoV that caused the SARS epidemic in 2003.
